services.name: postgresql-x64-18
services.note: observe-only: postmaster uptime is audit-round gate evidence, never auto-restart

mount.note: Checked via Win32_LogicalDisk, never Get-Volume: WinFsp/rclone volumes report MISSING to Get-Volume. The rclone mount process is the real server behind the letter.

sync.note: Freshness thresholds: a silent PC outage or tunnel drop leaves the last manifest on disk, so mtime age is the only liveness signal. Age over SLA is WARN; a wedged channel already FAILs at pchannel. cross_host_visible_sec is measured (10.3s with --vfs-cache-mode full + --dir-cache-time 10s), so a write made on one host needs >=12s before another host may read it back. churn_globs lists high-frequency state files owned by other subsystems: Diff classifies them as CHURN (reported, never quarantined, never rc=1), so real drift is not buried in expected noise. stale_manifest_recheck makes Diff re-read the live file before calling a hash mismatch DIVERGED: the ECS snapshot is written on an earlier round than the PC snapshot, so a write that lands in between makes the two manifests disagree while the file is already correct. Such entries are classified STALE_MANIFEST (reported, never quarantined, never rc=1); stale_manifest_max bounds the extra hashing so a mass break degrades to plain DIVERGED instead of a full re-hash. The same live re-check also covers the mirror case: when the PC snapshot is older than a write that has already landed here, no snapshot can judge the pair, so it is classified PENDING_SNAPSHOT (reported, never quarantined, never rc=1) and the next PC manifest round settles it -- a mismatch that survives a fresh snapshot still falls through to DIVERGED, so real drift is never masked for more than one round.

self_update.note: Step 0 of the daemon: compare the local toolchain with the PC mirror and pull newer copies, so a fix published once reaches every ECS box without manual work on the PC side. Fail-closed: a candidate must pass the PS parser (or be valid JSON) and byte-match after copy, the previous file is kept as .bak-<ts>, and any error silently skips the whole step.

guard.note: enum_shrink_* guard RemoteManifest against a wrong or half-dead remote root: a round enumerating fewer files than min_files, or fewer than (previous published count x ratio), is REFUSED - nothing is published and the hash cache is not pruned - because rc=0 on an empty root used to fabricate a full pc_only/ecs_only drift report and wipe the coverage cache in one round. A legitimate bulk delete therefore needs either a tiny previous count or an explicit ratio change.

ecs_hash.note: ECS-side SHA256 computed by actually reading the mount (SFTP lsjson returns no hashes). Bounded per run; the state cache fills coverage across daemon rounds.

fleet.note: Outside view across nodes: a node whose toolchain predates the daemon's step 0 self-update never upgrades, so it keeps publishing manifests without sha/md5 and without the stale/host fields, and its own Diff can only compare size/mtime while looking normal. Fleet reads every manifest-*.json in the shared dir and reports per node: generation (legacy = no stale/host field, or sha_coverage below min_sha_coverage), sha_coverage, and snapshot age. Results go to fleet-status.json plus TA-FLEET-ALERT lines in the ledger; exit 2 = at least one node legacy/stale/unreadable/missing, never a silent pass. expected_nodes is the fleet size to register (PC + 3 ECS); a shortfall is reported as MISSING_NODE, not as a failure of the nodes that did register.
